meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-25 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 1h 8m | Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Citrine VP Eng), Daniel Park (CTO), Samir Khan (DevOps), Aisha Rahman (Security)
summary: Kickoff for Citrine BioWorks onboarding — discuss deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC), pilot scope (6 weeks), success metrics (latency, cost per token, reliability) and next steps to start a staging pilot. Agreed to short infra deep-dive, share security artifacts, and set up staging access for benchmark runs.
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Alright everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off with quick intros and then go through the onboarding plan.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya here, VP Eng at Citrine. We're excited to move from eval to pilot, multiple stakeholders but primarily infra + security.
[00:20] Marco Diaz: Hey I'm Marco on the SE side — I'll own benchmarks and runtime tuning. Quick note, please forgive any transcription typos, sometimes Redwood Privat shows up as Redwood private or...
[00:36] Daniel Park: (laughs) we've seen that.
[00:38] Olivia Chen: Great. First question for Citrine — what's the current stack and expected QPS? Priya?
[00:46] Priya Nair: We run our inference layer in GCP, mostly GKE backed services. Peak conversational QPS around 45 across a handful of models. For the pilot we want to target 10 QPS steady with spikes to 60 for load tests. Latency target is p95 under 250ms for short responses. Cost targets are important — our finance lead wants a 30% cost reduction vs our current hosted vendor.
[01:10] Marco Diaz: Good context. With Redwood, common pattern is start hosted for speed then transition to Dedicated or Private for predictability. For the pilot we can run in your staging VPC with Redwood Private control plane or use a Redwood-hosted sneak preview; both are possible.
[01:28] Samir Khan: We prefer VPC peering — we can't forward prod data outside our network for compliance.
[01:34] Aisha Rahman: We're SOC2 aligned and will need KMS integration and audit logs. We'll also want RBAC scoping so only certain service accounts can call models.
[01:44] Marco Diaz: Absolutely — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and integrates with HSMs. Audit logs and token-level traces are available in the Console. One caveat: for initial benchmark runs we sometimes use ephemeral staging keys — so we'll need a short exception or a safe pattern for that.
[02:03] Priya Nair: Noted. What about model variants and fallback — if a large model has capacity issues how do we failover?
[02:10] Olivia Chen: We support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants. You can define a policy based on latency or cost and have automatic downgrades with graceful degradation.
[02:18] Daniel Park: Can we pin versions? We need deterministic outputs for regulatory audit.
[02:22] Marco Diaz: Yes — version pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B) are supported. We'll show you in the deep-dive.
[02:30] Leah Park: From the success side, we'll track quality regressions tied to prompt sets — Redwood Optimize can alert if model changes affect your tests.
[02:38] Priya Nair: Ok great. For the pilot, key success criteria: 1) p95 < 250ms on selected prompt set, 2) cost per 1k tokens under target, 3) no PII leakage per our evals.
[02:52] Marco Diaz: We'll need a canonical prompt set and synthetic load profile to run.
[02:57] Samir Khan: I'll put together a traffic replay and sample prompts. Expect a repo link by tomorrow.
[03:02] Aisha Rahman: On compliance, we need a SOC2 statement and encryption-at-rest details. Also question about data retention — can we control log retention and turn off user content retention?
[03:12] Olivia Chen: Yes, retention controls are configurable per-tenant and per-route. You can turn off persistent user content retention for the pilot; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[03:20] Daniel Park: Network-wise, what's required for peering? Ports, NAT, egress?
[03:24] Marco Diaz: We'll send a VPC network checklist. Typical reqs: egress to Redwood control plane hosts over TLS, a small set of IPs for peering, and optional TCP ports for health checks. If you're doing private on-prem we'll adjust the checklist.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Any blockers for us with GKE?
[03:41] Marco Diaz: Not really — we integrate via VPC peering and an IAM role for the staging service account. For dedicated GPU pools we may request a small baseline of capacity; otherwise hosted runs are immediate.
[03:52] Olivia Chen: Pricing — for the pilot we're proposing a 6-week pilot with a reduced committed capacity rate and a small engineering time retainers. I'll put the exact numbers in the follow-up.
[04:03] Priya Nair: Sounds good. We will need procurement terms for review.
[04:06] Olivia Chen: We'll include an easy pilot SOW and security addendum.
[04:10] Samir Khan: Benchmarking — what performance knobs should we expect to tune?
[04:14] Marco Diaz: Batching, KV cache settings (the transcription sometimes reads it as K V cash), sequence length tuning, and quantization profile if you go for lower memory footprints. Also kernel selection for GPUs matters.
[04:27] Aisha Rahman: On quantization — does that impact output determinism? We need consistent outputs for medical content.
[04:33] Marco Diaz: Slightly. We recommend running model evals with the quantized variant before promotion; Redwood Optimize can flag any semantic regressions.
[04:41] Priya Nair: How long to get the staging benchmark running if we give access today?
[04:46] Marco Diaz: Assuming we get staging VPC peering and sample prompts, initial runs within 48 hours. Full load tests and tuning in 7–10 days.
[04:55] Olivia Chen: Recap — we'll send pilot SOW, security docs, and VPC checklist. Marco will own benchmark plan; Aisha and Samir will provide security/network artifacts. Leah will run onboarding cadence.
[05:07] Daniel Park: Do you have a list of required personas for meetings? We want to loop in product and compliance owners.
[05:13] Leah Park: Yes, we'll share a 6-week cadence and invite template: weekly syncs, infra deep-dive, and a go/no-go review at week 5.
[05:21] Priya Nair: One more item — data residency. Can we ensure logs and metrics remain in EU for certain routes?
[05:27] Marco Diaz: Yes, routing by region and retention policies can keep telemetry and logs in the EU region. We'll document that.
[05:33] Aisha Rahman: Encryption keys — do you integrate with our Azure Key Vault?
[05:37] Marco Diaz: We support KMS integrations across major clouds — Azure Key Vault included. We'll need a short-lived credential for the initial bind.
[05:44] Samir Khan: Cool. I'll provision a service account and share minimal IAM perms.
[05:48] Olivia Chen: Anything else from Citrine?
[05:50] Priya Nair: Not right now. We'll get the security docs and prompt set over.
[05:54] Olivia Chen: Great. We'll send meeting notes and action items. Thanks everyone.
[06:00] (end of call)

Notes: transcript contains natural speech stops, some crosstalk, and occasional mis-recognitions (product names or acronyms). The team emphasized compliance and deterministic outputs — good fit for Redwood Private but pilot will start staging with VPC peering.
